# Building the Technical Writing Function

**Period:** 2023–present
**Role:** Technical Writing Manager
**Organization:** Integrations → Platform Documentation

## Context

The company's technical writing function had no centralized leadership. Technical writers were distributed across organizations with inconsistent processes, no shared vision, and limited coordination on site-wide documentation projects. This was the first dedicated technical writing management role at the company.

The management opportunity emerged after the 2023 layoffs reduced the technical writing team to five writers. With no other technical writer willing or able to step into a people leadership role, the business needed someone who could maintain delivery on critical commitments — compliance documentation, board-level integration guides, and an international product launch. I wrote the business case for the role and was formally promoted to L3 manager in Q4 FY2023.

The team I built and led was globally distributed: two full-time technical writers based in Japan, one senior technical writer based in the U.S., two contract technical writers based in Tokyo, and two contract technical writers based in the U.S. — six contributors spanning multiple time zones, organizational homes, and employment structures.

## Challenge

Define and execute the vision for the technical writing function across the entire company while navigating two major reorganizations, multiple manager changes, and expanding scope to include Knowledge Management — all while building and managing a globally distributed team of full-time and contract writers across the U.S. and Japan, without disrupting delivery or team morale.

## Approach

**Establishing the function (2023):**
- Stepped up as the sole willing technical writing manager post-layoffs; wrote the business case for the role and was promoted to L3.
- Created the INTEROPTW Jira project, onboarded new writers on process, Markdown, version control, and GitLab management, resolving 230+ INTEROPTW tickets.
- Managed documentation migration for the Developer Home launch — 4 product areas documented, exceeding the 80% migration target before end of July.
- Launched new integration tech docs (SuccessFactors, SmartRecruiters ATSs); contributed to 260+ installation guide completions by training technical writers to manage and create guides independently.
- Collaborated with Indeed Plus to align on a unified partner and developer platform, managing intake for documentation requests and driving strategic alignment across organizations.
- Managed 2 direct reports and 1 indirect report with 100% positive manager feedback score across all dimensions.

**Defining the function:**
- Defined priorities on the team wiki and established a draft vision presentation for technical writing.
- Surveyed technical writers to understand capacity and growth opportunities.
- Renamed the team Jira project to reflect the new organizational identity and sourced cross-org documentation project opportunities.
- De-risked the translation process by coordinating with two Japan-based full-time technical writers to document the translation workflow and define legal review responsibilities. Oversaw publication of a Canadian French product guide.
- Drove alignment with a self-serve product team by establishing 1:1 mentorship with U.S.-based contract writers and improving transparency through Jira dashboards.

**Scaling delivery:**
- Enabled launch of public documentation for an internal data tools platform — 4 product areas documented. Presented strategy at an onsite in Tokyo, defined the contribution process, and developed a long-term vision for scaling documentation support.
- Completed phase 1 of a site-wide information architecture revamp: reorganized documentation, reduced clutter, and created comprehensive getting started content for GraphQL and testing environments.
- Transitioned all integration documentation to the public site, eliminating the need for engineers to maintain multiple versions and unblocking the knowledge management team from adding an AI assistant.
- Partnered with operations teams to define job requirements, conduct interviews, and hire 2 contract technical writers based in Tokyo to support the new platform documentation area.

**Leading through change:**
- Assumed managerial responsibility for 2 U.S.-based contract writers from another team — helping hire, onboard, and integrate them — unifying a previously split function under a single strategy.
- Advocated for the team's organizational move to align with the engineering team responsible for the documentation site.
- Implemented weekly syncs, async standups, and code review rules to maintain coordination across U.S. and Japan time zones.
- Provided coaching and guidance through 2 reorganizations, maintaining delivery continuity across a geographically distributed team.
- Owned the full performance management cycle: wrote evaluations for FTEs and contractors using a structured H1/H2 review framework, ran calibration sessions with senior leadership, made bonus distribution decisions, and served as designated compensation manager.
- Managed vendor payments with a Japanese staffing company for Tokyo-based contract writers.

**Continued strategic leadership (2025–present):**
- Transitioned from people manager to senior IC in July 2025 and continue to serve as the strategic lead for the technical writing function.
- Wrote a team charter and strategy document that secured VP-level buy-in, establishing a shared direction for the function. Presented strategy at the AIX Q3 Town Hall and delivered a Technical Writing Primer/Vision document to align stakeholders on the function's direction.
- Defined and measured two key results (KRs) for the team, owning both goal-setting and outcome tracking.
- Proposed and secured leadership buy-in for a Japanese API documentation coverage KR; drove coverage to 88%, exceeding the 50% target. Led epic ownership, coordinated ticket workflow, and mentored a technical writer through execution.
- Analyzed 199 partner documentation feedback records and authored a report with 14 actionable recommendations for improving triage and feedback linking.
- Restructured Jira processes, decreasing average issue resolution time by 23.55% (from 34.49 to 26.37 days). Introduced issue-type tracking, established new triage cadence and sprint management practices, and set a 12-day average resolution baseline for cross-team requests.

**Knowledge Management expansion:**
- Organized and facilitated a Knowledge Management onsite in Tokyo — bringing together the Japan-based writing team and Knowledge Management stakeholders to align on a unified strategy.
- Presented proposed information architecture improvements to the Japan-based team.
- Collaborated with senior program management on knowledge transfer and cross-team communication.
